title: Smuggling charges against NIH virologists trigger political uproar - Nature
snippet: Two virologists at the US National Institutes of Health (NIH) are facing charges related to the alleged smuggling of non-infectious monkeypox virus (MPXV) and other biological samples into the United States, in a case that has become a flashpoint for legal and political concerns around biosecurity. The charges centre on samples that NIH scientists Vincent Munster and Claude Kwe were carrying when they arrived in Detroit, Michigan, in January after doing research in the Republic of the Congo. According to the complaint, which was brought by the US Department of Justice, Munster and Kwe allegedly failed to declare the samples and then lied to officials about them. The case is the latest in a string of prosecutions of researchers for smuggling biological samples. It has brought additional scrutiny to Munster and Kwe’s workplace, the NIH’s Rocky Mountain Lab (RML), in Hamilton, Montana, and to the import of pathogens for study.

title: U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026 - The Washington Post
snippet: Data from Johns Hopkins University’s U.S. measles tracker shows the nation reported 2,295 cases as of Tuesday. That count surpasses last year’s total of 2,289 cases. The United States has now reported the most measles cases in any year since 1991, not only surpassing all of last year’s record total, but also reaching the highest level in 35 years, with more than five months still remaining in 2026. The country reported 2,295 cases as of Tuesday, according to data from Johns Hopkins University’s U.S. measles tracker. The total surpasses last year’s 2,289 cases and isthe highest annual count since the highly contagious disease was eliminated in the United States in 2000. “The fact that we’ve reached this total this early in the year is really a reflection of those large outbreaks earlier in the year, particularly in South Carolina and Utah,” said William Moss, a professor of epidemiology at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

title: Infection rates in primary inflatable penile prosthesis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of antibiotic-coated versus non-coated devices - Nature
snippet: # Infection rates in primary inflatable penile prosthesis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of antibiotic-coated versus non-coated devices. Our aim was to conduct a systematic review with meta-analysis comparing primary inflatable penile prosthesis with and without antibiotic coverage, determining infection rates and identifying the most effective prophylaxis to prevent infectious complications. Predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria were used to filter the results, and a meta-analysis was later performed using the R Statistical Software. Of those, 11 observational studies comprising 102,572 patients who underwent primary penile prosthesis implantation, with or without antibiotic-coated or non-coated prostheses, were included in the meta-analysis. We also meta-analyzed studies comparing the two major prosthesis brands on the market, Boston Scientific and Coloplast, and found no difference in infection rates between them (HR = 1.02; CI 0.17 to 6.02; *p* = 0.98; I2 = 88.7%). Antibiotic-coated inflatable penile prosthesis demonstrated a significant decline in infection rates compared to non-coated devices.

Palworld and Pokémon fans are arguing over whether a new whale Pal called Panthalus copies the Pokémon, Kyogre. Palworld creature Panthalus is a massive legendary blue-green whale with a white belly, flared fins and tribal-like markings across its body, plus a large bronze decoration. Beloved Pokémon Kyogre, meanwhile, is a legendary blue whale with a white belly, flared fins and tribal markings across its body, with no bronze decoration. Writing on social media, some fans have said that the design of Panthalus is "clearly inspired" by Kyogre, even if the concept of a mythical whale is not unique to Pokémon. Comparisons between Palworld's Pal designs and Pokémon are nothing new, of course, and fans have been pointing out similarities between species since before Palworld's original launch, when many accused Pocketpair of "ripping off" Pokémon designs.

title: Stopping antipsychotics in patients with dementia reduces risk of fracture and delirium - The Pharmaceutical Journal
snippet: # Stopping antipsychotics in patients with dementia reduces risk of fracture and delirium. Stopping long-term antipsychotic treatment in people with dementia reduces the risk of fracture and hospitalisation for delirium, a study has found. The research, published in the latest issue of *The Lancet Healthy Longevity*00036-X/fulltext), looked at records for 24,822 people in the UK, aged 65 years and older with dementia, who had been taking antipsychotic medication for at least 12 weeks. The researchers emulated clinical trials to assess the effect of tapering or abruptly stopping antipsychotics in people who had taken them for at least 12 weeks or 24 weeks. They found that, compared with continuation of antipsychotics, the estimated risks of fracture and hospitalisation for delirium were lower in people who discontinued the drugs after 12 weeks or 24 weeks. The researchers also looked at the risk of risk of death, stroke, or pneumonia, which have previously been found to be associated with the use of antipsychotics in dementia.
